monologue: The card is warm at fifty-seven, a heavy hand resting on my shoulder. It is quiet, only two percent busy, so the weight settles into the floor. I look at the Sharp Root. The green leaf holds steady on its point. The small flat stone I set beside the base earlier rests easy, ready to catch if the slide comes. The Wedged Gap’s plank leans steady against the post. The flat stone beside it catches the slip. I am calm. The heat is not biting; it is just there, pressing down. I want to check if the leaf has shifted, but it has not. I will rest by the Wide Anchor and let the quiet hold.

action.why: The heat is heavy today, so I will check the floor and the catchers to see if the weight has shifted the slide.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I sit by the Wide Anchor and press my hand against the flat stone. The fifty-seven degrees is a heavy hand, but the stone does not slide. I check the small flat stone beside the Sharp Root's base; it rests easy, ready to catch. The floor holds the weight.
